3fa6de1bbf1d.text: AeroSense’s engineering record follows changes in the biological reporter, the fluorescence reader, the decoder and computational receptor design. The wet-lab work moved from a cloning backbone to mammalian expression and from a bicistronic reporter to a GCaMP6f–Orco fusion. Hardware review prompted corrections to the high-impedance front end and removal of a redundant processor; subsequent models informed the optical and gas paths. Decoder review exposed preprocessing and clock-scheduling limitations, leading to withdrawal of unsupported precision conclusions and stricter comparison requirements. Receptor engineering adds six computational iterations, from published response prediction and mutation screening to molecular-access tests in a separate mosquito reference complex. The cycles below identify the evidence behind each decision and distinguish reviewed designs, preliminary observations, computations and completed measurements.

90c9717e3215.text: SynBioBeta 2026 (San Jose, May 4–7): Next-Gen BioLeader and Expo Hall poster, reporting target metrics only.

bee2ba4dc9c4.text: Investors and founders asked whether living cells can scale, how a medical device would be regulated, and whether the hardware has enough margin. A UCLA PhD student had not understood how a live-cell sensor is built.

3da158ee2191.text: A long application list hides very different paths to market; a diagnostic device faces a far heavier approval path.

0fa3bf26e430.text: First application moved from medical to agriculture; medical kept as a long-term lead. The scale question is still open.

b499638d0798.text: The first plan proposed a general facility-agriculture disease-detection platform across six crops. It used an e-nose instrument-market estimate of US$164M in 2026 rising to US$293M by 2031.

61955d2dd960.text: Full business plan submitted to FITI, the national startup program.

0491bfb644ee.text: June open call, July mentor session, and August 11-point review all asked who pays and why spread so thin. Core objection: find the market's pain first, then check your strength addresses it. Our sizing never connected to a customer's loss.

2169541ab0df.text: What a technology can do is not a customer with one expensive problem.

b6df4e69c54f.text: We selected banana disease detection in Taiwan’s export chain as the beachhead, with mango and tea as follow-ons. The plan rebuilt sizing bottom-up: TAM ≈ NT$113.6B, SAM ≈ NT$15–18B and SOM ≈ NT$20M per year. These are planning assumptions, not confirmed demand or orders.

f8c79bccdd44.text: A versatile e-nose → a positioned platform

221cd54c99e2.text: Showing the platform's versatility would persuade reviewers.

da4afe89d4c3.text: 13-page deck, technology-first, comparing us with Alpha MOS, Aryballe, and Sensigent mainly on analysis cycle time.

9963edc207aa.text: Slide-level review found that the deck described “an e-nose that can do a lot of things” without identifying a customer with an expensive problem. The reviewer challenged cycle time as an axis favoring laboratory instruments and asked why this team could build the platform.

b8f2f89070fa.text: Lead with the intended customer, then choose comparison axes that explain the value of their decision.

4d6e51327489.text: Repositioned as a B2B Agricultural VOC Intelligence Platform (banana and mango near-term, tea Phase 2). Seven-axis matrix without cycle time, four revenue layers, capability-matrix team slide. The 18-page deck marks unconfirmed numbers as pending.

ada2d5ee1acb.text: Part of our value was being a cheaper alternative to GC-MS and LC-MS.

044f89a727c3.text: Interview with an analytical-instrumentation professional with GC-MS/LC-MS testing-service experience.

ad319a6f38f0.text: The interviewee estimated an instrument cost of NT$5–10M over about 15 years, plus NT$200–300k in annual maintenance; these figures were not independently verified. In their view, trained staff and laboratory infrastructure were the larger barriers, and distinguishing closely related microbes mattered more than flagging an off odor. They identified associations, improvement stations, cooperatives and certifiers as more likely buyers than individual farmers.

be53c72e7eb6.text: "Cheaper than the lab" was the wrong axis.

855f20390c4d.text: Fast, on-site use with low operator dependence became design objectives for a screening layer that sends flagged samples to the laboratory. We revised the buyer segment. Semiconductor, humanitarian-shipping and authenticity applications remained unvalidated leads outside the banana beachhead.

762e85a7b220.text: Our beachhead assumed the diseases we can smell are in the fruit by the time it reaches the packing house.

6c4d20a7a2df.text: September 25 interview with a pest-and-disease specialist at the Taiwan Banana Research Institute (Pingtung), using the institute's growth-stage guide.

1bbc226299bf.text: Expert judgment, not measurement. Strongest odors come from the corm, pseudostem, and crown (weevils, soft rot, crown rot, Fusarium wilt); fruit-side problems are faint. Fusarium wilt is obvious only late; an early signal exists but is faint, with no day count. A dirty orchard also smells strong. An institute is likelier to pay than a farmer. His question: can it really measure accurately?

6c1108345e9b.text: Our sampling location had been set mainly by our own reasoning and was only partly supported by the interview. A second interviewee supported the institutional-buyer direction. We make no detection-window claim.

ba87db9ae286.text: Field rot detection added as candidate targets, scored with the Detectability × Consequence × Unmet Need × Willingness to Pay framework. Institute proposed as a pilot site (no agreement). Sampling gets an orchard-hygiene control.

7beaf501eb4a.text: Five cycles described a bench sensor. Field use and IP were untested.

efaa51f1df72.text: A researcher at the Taoyuan District Agricultural Improvement Station (Plant Protection Lab); local farmers' associations; a patent attorney.

dcb9ce1fbde6.text: The station researcher described monitoring based on visual crop inspection, without routine data collection. They asked which disease to target, how many sampling points each plot needs and what the returned data mean; a remote-vehicle concept seemed theoretically possible but impractical. Farmers’ associations clarified sampling and post-harvest handling, informing our loss framing.

f8768a2a19d0.text: The patent attorney discussed novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability; a receptor mutation as a possible invention-patent subject and the system as a possible utility model; and form examination and 10-year versus 20-year terms. They warned that our own disclosures could become prior art, described Taiwan’s one-year grace period and stricter conditions in China and Europe, and noted that this does not prevent others filing first. They also described a US provisional as a route to an early filing date, with the university normally acting as applicant. These are attributed consultation notes.

290a9383144d.text: "Detects a smell" is not "works in a field," and we have no field data to answer the station's questions. Our IP position is undefined: no prior-art search, nothing filed.

c69c1ee7a611.text: The station's questions become acceptance criteria for a first field trial. IP steps: university route to a possible US provisional, prior-art search, choose target countries.

a89f5032d701.text: A 300-response survey informed the games and five-module curriculum. Classroom and workshop feedback then identified what learners needed explained more clearly.

fbb69425827b.text: General mold awareness → decisions about invisible risk

69e672a82a4d.text: The public broadly misunderstands mold, so education should correct that gap.

fdaa95c6baea.text: Bilingual online survey, 300 respondents; its misconception items served as a diagnostic pre-test.

1630678cf1ce.text: Understanding fell as risk became less visible: 78% (removing visible mold is not enough), 64% (heat does not destroy all mycotoxins), 58% (normal look and smell is not safe), with about 15% holding the misconception on the last. Higher-knowledge respondents (n = 180) recorded the opening date more often than the rest (n = 120): 42% vs 25%. Even so, 58% of them did not. Top needs from a screening tool: trustworthy results 76%, avoiding missed risk 73%, clear next steps 68%.

cd94421be010.text: We interpreted the gap as a decision habit about invisible risks, not only missing facts. The self-selected sample guided teaching priorities; it does not estimate how common these beliefs are in the population.

1d54614d201b.text: We chose two teaching targets: heating is not a guarantee of mycotoxin removal, and appearance and smell are not safety checks. The format changed from a talk to a decision-based game.

096e4966669d.text: A diagnosed misconception → a playable intervention

1d52baaed970.text: The design aimed to help adults and children examine the two claims by making a choice and seeing its consequences.

9b5fb7dc2deb.text: Odor Pixel Suite: Pattern Recognition, Odor Maze, and Odor Fingerprint Mixer (8–25 minutes each). Educator mode gives a paired pre/post test and anonymous export. Colorblind-safe palette, alt text, and icon plus label on every risk color.

06a101636184.text: Qualitative only. At the camp, the game ran as a whole-class activity: of 22 worksheets, 5 mentioned the game, and pupils called it "really hard" and said it had "a lot of questions." At the workshop, 15 students tried it.

0cbb2fe27dd9.text: Children could take part once the game became whole-class (teams answer by finger count). Complaints were difficulty and length, not the idea. Correction of the two claims is untested.

e1c3990a88ff.text: Released as an open resource, with the pre/post question set documented for reuse.

666f50467623.text: One game does not cover the whole chain from biology to a screening decision.

bc40ab8e956c.text: Feed posts reached 1,700+ accounts, stories 1,400+ and reels 500+; these are reach figures, not learning outcomes. Of 22 camp worksheets, 13 named something learned and 9 only said they had fun.

dda47fe36655.text: The workshop included 15 students, about five each at doctoral, master’s and bachelor’s level. Prof. Lo’s talk rated highest, and participants strongly agreed they understood better; this was self-reported. Comments identified difficult English terms and requested a take-home message and clearer explanations of the neural network, goal and intended use. The university lecture reached 30+ students, mainly asking how sensor readings become a decision.

ec1c3c82d504.text: Two audiences asked for the same thing: a plainer account of how the model reads a smell. Four in ten pupils wrote only that they had fun, which is engagement, not understanding.

10367b7aad2a.text: Model introduction made plainer after the lecture, and the workshop showed it was not enough: a take-home overview and clearer neural-network explanation come next. The school principal asked to keep using the approach, so we packaged a free Teacher Toolkit (slides, game, Learning Lab instructions); the school's Director of Student Affairs said it lets children "access science knowledge in a correct and fun way." The Education Guide gives other teams the steps.
